setups.quote: This result is corroborated by numerical experiments carried out on synthetic problems as well as on instances of the Max-Cut problem, which show that our method performs better than plain simulated annealing when large barren plateaus are present in the domain.

IV we showcase an application of our Fleming-Viot inspired algorithm for a synthetic problem with varying percentages of barren plateaus in the parameter landscape, as well as an application to a Quantum Approximation Optimization Algorithm (QAOA, a special case of VQA) for an instance of the Max-Cut problem on a graph with 8 nodes.
(i) two-dimensional synthetic functions generated with a predefined percentage of barren plateaus; (ii) the Max-Cut problem approximated by a noiseless twodimensional quantum circuit.
Each synthetic experiment is defined by an expected percentage of barren plateaus in the optimization landscape whose domain is set as the two-dimensional rectangular area [0, 1] × [0, 1].

The precise definition of these three barren levels is given in Section IV-C. Each accepted1 synthetic function is classified into one of these barren levels based on the actual percentage of barren plateaus present in the function, estimated as described in App.
